name: St. Johann in Tirol
kurzbeschreibung: Village community in the Leukental valley between the Kaisergebirge and Kitzbüheler Alpen – pure active holiday.
beschreibung:
Overview

St. Johann in Tirol is located at an elevation of 659 meters in the Leukental valley within the Kitzbühel district. Positioned at the confluence of three rivers forming the Großache, the town nestles at the northeastern foot of Mount Kitzbüheler Horn (1,996 m), enjoying unobstructed views of the jagged Wilder Kaiser range. With roughly 9,900 inhabitants, this historic market town is the most populous municipality in the Kitzbühel district. St. Johann effortlessly merges alpine town vibrancy with authentic Tyrolean warmth: a pedestrianized center with colorful painted townhouses, historic brewing traditions at Huber Bräu, and weekly markets sits alongside the diverse SkiStar St. Johann in Tirol ski domain and scenic trails in the Kitzbühel Alps.

History

Human settlement dates back to Celtic copper miners in the 4th century BC at Rerobichl. During the 16th and 17th centuries, copper and silver mining flourished, with the Holy Spirit shaft plunging nearly 900 meters underground, celebrated at the time as the deepest mine shaft in the world. The town was first documented between 1150 and 1160 as sancti Johannis in Liuckentale. Until 1808, St. Johann served as the summer residence of the Prince-Bishops of Chiemsee, and was granted market town status in 1956. The town's crowning landmark is the Deanery Church of the Assumption, universally known as the Cathedral of the Leukental due to its twin-towered facade and monumental scale, erected between 1723 and 1728 by Bavarian master builder Abraham Millauer and adorned with frescoes by Simon Benedikt Faistenberger.

Getting there

St. Johann in Tirol functions as the premier transport junction of the northeastern Tyrolean Unterland. By car, state road B178 (Loferer Straße) connects swiftly to the A12 motorway at Wörgl or Kufstein, as well as toll-free from Salzburg. State road B161 leads south to Kitzbühel (just 10 km away) and the Pass Thurn, while the B164 connects east to Fieberbrunn and Zell am See. Rail travelers enjoy direct InterCity and EuroCity express train services calling at St. Johann in Tirol railway station on the Salzburg-Tyrol mainline, linking directly to Vienna, Salzburg, Munich, and Innsbruck. Extensive regional bus routes connect throughout the valleys.

Tips

In winter, ski the northern slopes of the Kitzbüheler Horn in the SkiStar St. Johann ski area, accessing 43 kilometers of groomed pistes up to Harschbichl (1,604 m), which commands the finest close-up panorama of the Wilder Kaiser. During summer, families head to the Hornpark high ropes course at the mid-station, featuring eight climbing circuits and a zipline across the mountain lake, before descending on mountain carts. Hike through the spectacular Grießbachklamm gorge in nearby Erpfendorf along hanging bridges and waterfalls. In the town center, visit the 27-meter-high Huber Bräu brewery tower for fresh beer and sweeping views, or browse local delicacies at the Friday morning farmers' market.
